patch_description:
This design replaces the log-sum-exp softmin/softmax surrogate used by the previous programs with a fundamentally different smooth, scale-invariant objective: the "moment product" f_q = log(Σ s^q) + log(Σ s^{-q}) over squared pair distances s. As q → ∞, minimizing f_q drives dmax² down and dmin² up simultaneously (q-th moments of s and 1/s approximate the extremes), and it is exactly scale-invariant for every q, so it forms a natural homotopy: small q optimizes globally-smooth average-based geometry, large q sharpens toward the true min/max ratio. Gradients are computed stably in log-space via logsumexp-style softmax weights (no overflow for large q).

The pipeline is organized as budget-tiered screening (inspired by the runtime-reduction recommendation): (1) a cheap screen anneals q ∈ {0.6, 2.5} with short L-BFGS-B runs over ~21 diverse structured seeds (staggered hexagonal double-rings with poles, icosahedron+poles, cube+face-pushes, antipodal 7-direction pairs, and repulsion-spread randoms via a Coulomb-like descent); (2) only the top 5 basins receive the deep anneal (q ∈ {6, 20}) plus the exact nonsmooth (dmin/dmax)² gradient polish with decaying jitter restarts; (3) the top 2 candidates get a final epigraph SLSQP stage that directly maximizes t subject to t ≤ |x_i−x_j|² ≤ 1 (the exact mathematical program for the problem, with a vectorized 182-row constraint Jacobian), which can squeeze marginal gains beyond what the kinked L-BFGS objective reaches. All stages compare on the exact true ratio, keep the best, and the result is normalized so dmax = 1.
